claims.claim_ar: الفعل «قُلْ» فعل أمر يفتتح الخطاب ويستخدم لاستئناف الكلام الموجه إلى المخاطبين.
claims.claim_en: The verb «قُلْ» is an imperative that opens the address and functions to resume/direct speech to the addressees.

claims.source_quote_ar: كلام مستأنف مسوق للرجوع إلى مخاطبتهم
claims.claim_ar: الافتتاح بـ«قُلْ تَعَالَوْا أَتْلُ...» نمط استئنافي مسوَّق يبیّن رجوعَ المخاطب إليه مباشرةً (عودة المخاطبة)، أي تحول الأسلوب إلى مخاطبة صريحة.
claims.claim_en: The opening «قُل تَعَالَوْا أَتْلُ...» is a resumptive (mustanfa) formula that signals a return to direct address (an explicit shift back to addressing the audience).
claims.needs_review_reason: The quoted source speaks of a similar resumptive return-to-address in a different verse; applying it to this ayah is by analogy and should be verified against classical tafsirs focused specifically on S6:151.

claims.source_quote_ar: كرره مع قرب ذكره زيادة في التأكيد
claims.claim_ar: تكرار النفي/النهي («وَلَا تَقْتُلُوا ... وَلَا تَقْرَبُوا ...») يعمل كرَكْرَة بلاغية لزيادة التأكيد والتحذير.
claims.claim_en: Repetition of prohibitive particles/commands (e.g., the recurring «وَلَا تَقْتُلُوا», «وَلَا تَقْرَبُوا») functions as a rhetorical repetition to heighten emphasis and warning.
claims.needs_review_reason: Source remark about repetition is given for a different prophetic utterance; mapping to the specific repeated negations in this ayah is plausible but should be cross-checked with verse-specific commentary.

claims.claim_ar: تتابع الجمل والأوامر المرتبطة بـ«و» يدلّ على ربطٍ واستئنافٍ بين بنود النهي؛ الواو هنا تعمل كأداة عطف/استئناف تربط أحكامًا متعددة.
claims.claim_en: The repeated conjunction «و» functions as an associative/resumptive conjunction linking the successive prohibitions and instructions; the waw acts as a connective/continuative device.
claims.needs_review_reason: The source notes the function of the waw in other syntactic contexts; identifying each waw in this ayah as 'استئنافية' requires closer verse-level syntactic analysis.

warnings: Source chunks provided are general grammatical/tafsir excerpts and sometimes discuss rhetorical features illustrated with other verses. Several claims above are inferred by analogy from those discussions to S6:151; please verify each claim against verse-specific tafsir/بلاغة sources.

Some device assignments (e.g., labeling particular 'و' as استئنافية or treating repetition strictly as بديع/تكرار) involve interpretive judgement that may vary among commentators; such cases are marked with lower confidence and a reasons for review.

Fields 'root' and 'lemma' are left null where no clear single-word root/lemma applies (e.g., iltifat or conjunction-level devices). If you prefer a different encoding for function words, indicate the desired convention.
